skill_traces.query:
Sam: Hey Evan! Exciting news: I started a new diet and exercise routine last Monday and it's made a huge difference. I feel great! What about you, what changes have you made recently?
Evan: Wow, Sam, great! Glad your new diet/exercise is going well. As for me, I've hit a sore spot lately. Twisted my knee last Friday and it's really painful, so it's been tough to stay consistent with my usual fitness routine. It's really frustrating because staying active is like, mega-important to me.
Sam: Oh no, sorry to hear about that, Evan. It's frustrating when our bodies don't cooperate, isn't it? Is there anything I can do to help?
Evan: Thanks, Sam. I appreciate the concern. Life throws us curveballs - that's life, right? By the way, remember that book I was talking about? It just gets better with every page, can't let it out of my hands!
Sam: Life sure can be unpredictable and tough. Being adaptable and finding other ways to stay active is key when you're facing an obstacle. Maybe look into low-impact exercises or physical therapy to help with that? And damn, you really got me interested in this book haha!
Evan: Yeah, PT for my knee is on the cards. Hopefully I'll get an appointment soon. Till then, just keeping it low-key and swimming to stay active.
Sam: Swimming is a good choice, Evan. It's low-impact and easy on the joints, plus it's refreshing. Keep up with the active lifestyle!
Evan: Yeah, thanks for the push, Sam. Oh, hey, I came across this pic when I was tidying up. I took a road trip last month - the scenery was stunning and nature really chilled me out.
Sam: Wow, looks great! Where did you go? Bet it was nice to get away.
Evan: Thanks! I went up to the Rocky Mountains, it was so refreshing! The views were stunning and I felt so relaxed. Do you enjoy road trips and exploring nature?
Sam: I haven't gone on a road trip in ages, but I love being surrounded by nature. It's so tranquil and refreshing. I'd love to go hiking more, but it can be a bit challenging sometimes. However, I am working on becoming healthier, so maybe a road trip and a hike will be possible soon.
Evan: That's cool, Sam. Nature can be really peaceful. I'd suggest going for more hikes, like I do. It's always been calming and fun. We should definitely do one together sometime.
Sam: Sounds like fun! Which lake do you recommend? I'd love to explore some of the local trails.
Evan: Check out this one! It's gorgeous and there are lots of trails nearby. You'll love it!
Sam: Wow, it looks great! Is it nearby? What a view!
Evan: It's only a two-hour drive from here, but trust me, it's worth every minute for the incredible views and peaceful atmosphere.
Sam: Cool, a day trip's doable. Nature's calling me, so I'm gonna go check it out! Thanks!
Evan: No worries, enjoy your time in nature. Take care! Bye!
Sam: Thanks Evan. Have a good one. See ya!

selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.
